nodes.long_description:
**Sculpt clay out of thin air.** Clayground is a VR clay sculpting studio for Meta Quest, made by one independent artist. Push, pull, carve, smooth and paint volumetric clay with your hands, then take your work anywhere as a GLB or OBJ.

**Sculpt like it's real clay**
- Add, carve, pull, smooth, inflate, flatten, crease and paint, with strength control
- Mirror and radial symmetry for faces, creatures and patterns
- Layers you can hide, freeze, merge and change the resolution of: rough it in, then go fine
- Lattice: bend any part with a cage of handles
- Spline: draw a curve and get a tube, a hollow pipe, a row of stamps, or a cookie-cutter trim
- A starter stamp library, or capture your own stamps from your sculpts

**Bring it to life**
- Frame-by-frame animation and live-recorded motion; one-press Breathe, Sway and Boil
- Export animated GLBs

**In your room or in the studio**
- Mixed reality keeps your room in view, or sculpt in a calm virtual studio
- Up to 90 Hz on Quest 3 and 3S when your sculpt leaves room

**Take it anywhere**
- Export GLB with colour, or OBJ, for Blender, game engines, AR and 3D printing
- Pair with clayvr.com using a short code and grab your files over Wi-Fi, no cable

**Coming from Adobe Medium?** Clayground is made for you: volumetric clay, layers, stamps and a tool wheel, standalone on Quest.

Free in Early Access and updated often. Updates: clayvr.com · Support: Hey@emotionull.art
nodes.short_description: Sculpt, paint and animate clay with your hands on Meta Quest, no PC needed. Layers, symmetry, lattice, splines and stamps, in VR or mixed reality. Then export GLB or OBJ for Blender, game engines and 3D printing. Free, made by an independent artist.

nodes.long_description:
Clayground is true volumetric clay sculpting on Meta Quest.
Paint infinite clay with zero polygon anxiety, on an unbounded canvas that grows wherever you sculpt. Capture any part of your sculpt as a stamp. Sculpt in mixed-reality passthrough at your real desk. Export to Blender with one press.
nodes.short_description: Real clay. Your room. Sculpt without limits.

nodes.change_log:
All ten items from the Discord follow-ups and Yang’s report are fixed in 0.2.283. The Quest APK is built but not installed; nothing has been tried on the headset yet.

Report	Fix
“Saved my mushroom… overwrote my moon”	Save now asks first on a file you opened (“Save over ‘Moon’? Press Save again to replace it”). Save As opens the headset keyboard, makes a new file with a name that can’t clash, and leaves the original untouched. It replaces “Save New”.
Can’t start drawing on a low-res layer	On an empty layer, Res+ and Res− now apply instantly. The layer’s grid is rescaled around its centre, and a label shows the new detail size in mm.
Palette on the back of the off hand	Comfort > Palette now has three settings: Button, Flip, Always. Always shows the palette the moment the back of your off hand faces you, and every trigger pick sets the colour.
“No way to aim the camera!”	Photo is now a camera in your hand. A live preview screen floats above the tool controller and shows exactly what will be saved. Trigger shoots, stick zooms, B (or Photo again) puts it away. While it’s up the trigger never sculpts, and grips still turn the scene for framing.
“A tool called Move should move an object”	The dough tool is now called Pull. Layers > Move layer is how you move a whole piece, and the Pull tooltip points there.
Paint spills past the sphere	Paint used to reach about 35% beyond the brush sphere. It now stops at the sphere’s edge.
Freeze needs a tooltip; what are ^ / v?	Resting the pointer on Freeze, the ^ / v arrows or Move layer now explains what they do.
Zoom resolution label	Holding both grips to zoom shows the clay detail size, e.g. “6.3 mm voxels zoom 140%”.
Yang: GLB transparency lost, one shared material	Each layer now exports its own material, named after the layer. Glass stays see-through in Blender, glow exports as glow, and metal and roughness come from the layer. All the poses of one animated layer share one material.

Lattice no longer traps A and keeps your bend when you switch away.
Only your own saves appear in Files, and guests can't overwrite your sculpt.
The see-through holes (#3) came from the memory cleanup freeing parts of the clay that draw a neighbouring surface. They no longer open.
The colour change after lowering resolution (#5) came from that step halving the clay's depth information. Colours now hold when you keep sculpting.
Lowering resolution on an empty layer just says there's nothing to lower.
Menus no longer auto-close.
Pointing Select at empty space deselects.
Strokes fade out instead of cutting off.
Labels can stay on all the time.

Fixed and proven:
Lattice no longer traps the A button, and switching away keeps your bend.
A flips between your last two tools.
Only your own saves appear in Files; anything automatic goes to Files > Backups.
Lowering resolution on an empty layer just says there's nothing to lower.
Menus stay open unless you turn on auto-close.
Picking empty space with Select deselects.
Flipping your off hand over shows the palette.
Strokes fade out instead of cutting off.
Labels can stay on all the time.
The Tools page says which tools aren't on the wheel.
Built, only partly testable on desktop:
Bigger hint text that stays up longer.
Panels that are no longer see-through and don't interrupt a stroke you've started.
A colour per tool.
Rename and a colour chip for each layer.
Photo and backdrop colour.
The volume setting and softer sounds.
Not solved:
The see-through holes on the moon (#3). My first theory was disproved by a direct check of every triangle against the clay surface. The one improvement I kept takes a heavily pulled test blob from 12 to 10 bad triangles out of about 54,000; it isn't the player's case. Could you ask them for the moon .clay file? If we can't reproduce it, drawing both sides of the clay would hide these holes for certain, but it costs GPU time, so it needs your OK and a headset performance check first.
Colour shift after lowering resolution (#5). I couldn't reproduce it either, so I kept a safer colour pick but haven't claimed a fix.
Controller models (#8). These need Meta's Core SDK.

Fixed in this batch, each with a test that fails when its fix is switched off:

Undo now fully reverses layer operations. Merge down, Subtract, Intersect and Merge selected (including with 3+ layers) are each one undo press. The clay comes back exactly, voxel for voxel, instead of being doubled.
Split: one undo removes the piece and puts the clay back. The temporary scratch ball no longer bumps one of your deleted layers out of the 2-slot deleted-layer store.
Deleted layers stay undoable after you keep sculpting. Undo steps back through your strokes, then brings the layer back.
Too-old undos are refused. If a layer it needs has already been permanently cleared, Undo says so instead of doing half the job.
Moving a layer, reordering, then undoing reselects the layer that actually moved.
Delete with several layers ticked removes all of them ("Delete 3"), and one Undo brings them all back.
Files asks before destroying anything:
Save over and Del need a second press within 4 seconds; the button reads "Sure?" while waiting.
A failed save now says so, and no longer leaves the sculpt marked as saved.
Export leaves hidden layers out, including phone shares. An error partway through no longer jams exporting until restart.
Boot hitch: shader warm-up was saving an empty recording over the good one on every pause. It now keeps them separate, never saves a smaller recording, and logs whether recording works on the headset.
Device-log noise: the Lattice tool no longer logs every second, and the log's repeat filter now catches lines whose only difference is the numbers. The bounds warning that appeared whenever a layer was set aside to save memory is fixed, as is the new-layer behaviour that set the previous layer aside straight away.
Passthrough: shadows, see-through clay, panels and text were blending at a fraction of their intended strength (a 40% shadow showed at 16%). This is the one fix that still needs a look on the headset.
